extracted.intended_audience: machine learning / NLP researchers and practitioners working on generative language models and uncertainty quantification
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and calibrating conformal-prediction-style procedures for generative language models by sampling outputs, applying stopping/rejection rules, and providing statistical guarantees on the returned set (and on component-level correctness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prediction-set statistical guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard conformal prediction produces prediction sets -- in place of single predictions -- that have rigorous, statistical performance guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The produced set should satisfy coverage-style guarantees (e.g., contain at least one acceptable answer with high probability). This is the central formal requirement that motivates the calibration procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration of a sampling stopping rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibrate a stopping rule for sampling different outputs from the LM that get added to a growing set of candidates until we are confident that the output set is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stopping rule determines when to stop sampling; it must be calibrated (using held-out data / calibration) so that, together with other mechanisms, it supports the formal coverage guarantees while controlling sample cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration and application of a rejection rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneously calibrate and apply a rejection rule for removing candidates from the output set to reduce noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some sampled outputs may be low-quality, a rejection criterion is used to discard noisy candidates; this must be calibrated to avoid violating coverage guarantees while improving set precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: returned set contains an acceptable answer with high probability
rubrics_metrics.description: The sampled set returned by the procedure contains at least one acceptable answer with high probability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit coverage requirement is the concrete instantiation of the statistical guarantee; calibration and rules should be chosen to ensure this property holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical precision / small average set size
rubrics_metrics.description: While maintaining coverage guarantees, the method should be empirically precise (i.e., produce small output sets on average).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a tradeoff between guaranteeing coverage and producing small sets; metrics and evaluation should measure average set size and precision alongside coverage to assess practical usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component-level correctness identification (hallucination detection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the set of candidate responses, accurately identify subsets of individual components—such as phrases or sentences—that are each independently correct (e.g., that are not 'hallucinations'), with statistical guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approach should provide procedures and calibration to flag or certify correct subcomponents, enabling finer-grained assurance than whole-response coverage; evaluations should test phrase/sentence-level correctness and associated guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of conformal prediction to sampling over combinatorial output spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate conformal prediction to the setting where LM responses are sampled from the model's predicted distribution over the large, combinatorial output space of natural language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designing conformal methods for generative LMs requires handling sampling-based generation and combinatorial outputs (rather than simple classification outputs); methodology must account for sampling variability and large output support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task and model generality / empirical demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the approach's promise across multiple tasks (open-domain question answering, text summarization, radiology report generation) and different LM variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical evaluation should include diverse tasks and model families to show applicability and robustness; empirical results should report coverage, set size, and component-identification performance per task.
